title: Lee and Macron Agree on Hormuz Cooperation, Expand Defense Ties
detail: During a state visit to France marking the 140th anniversary of bilateral diplomatic ties, President Lee Jae-myung and President Emmanuel Macron held a summit at the Elysee Palace, agreeing to cooperate on restoring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz — which Macron described as a 'peaceful' multinational effort. Seoul stopped short of committing troops, saying it is 'reviewing various options, including military measures, but no deployment decision has been made,' amid an Iranian warning that military participation would be treated as support for U.S. action. The two sides also upgraded their military classified-information protection agreement, agreed to pursue a mutual military logistics support pact, and committed to defense-industry cooperation pairing France's technology with Korea's manufacturing base, including potential Airbus partnerships.

title: Samsung and Mistral AI Sign Partnership to Apply AI to Chip Production
detail: Samsung Electronics and French AI developer Mistral AI signed an MOU at the Elysee Palace, witnessed by President Lee Jae-myung and President Macron, under which Samsung is set to lead roughly €3 billion (~₩4.68 trillion) in investment and raise its stake in Mistral. Samsung plans to deploy Mistral's AI technology across its chip manufacturing floors to improve yields and process efficiency, particularly for sub-2-nanometer node production, part of a broader Korea-France 'advanced industries' alliance struck during Lee's state visit.

title: Korea Disaster Relief Team's First Foot Search in Nepal Yields No Results
detail: The Korea Disaster Relief Team conducted its first on-foot search in the Ramche area of Rasuwa district for the nine missing Korean nationals, after helicopters, drones and ground teams had failed to locate them. The search 'yielded no results'; steep terrain prevented safe helicopter landings and Nepalese authorities concluded that further tunnel searches at the Upper Trishuli-1 site were no longer feasible. An official said the team had 'done everything possible through foot searches within a safe range.' Recovery efforts elsewhere at the site had rescued one Chinese survivor and recovered several unidentified bodies, not yet confirmed as belonging to the missing Koreans.
